title: Button skeleton placeholder + optimistic UI announcement pattern for intermittent network latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Product teams continue to see edge regressions where a button transition from idle -> loading is visually abrupt during high-latency paths (mobile networks, cold caches). In several bug reports, users perceived actions as unregistered when the spinner appeared late; accessibility reviewers also flagged lack of timely ARIA live announcements for optimistic UI updates. This ticket proposes a design pattern: a lightweight, theme-aware skeleton affordance that appears immediately on tap/click for network-bound actions, paired with a short ARIA announcement and a stable layout strategy so buttons don't shift when content changes.

Scope: Design specs, token adjustments, and component guidance for: primary/secondary/ghost variants, icon-only and split buttons, text length changes, and dark/light theming. Include motion timing for skeleton fade and fallback behavior for interrupted requests (cancel/undo).

Goals:
- Reduce perceived latency by showing immediate tactile feedback without introducing new layout shifts.
- Ensure screen readers receive concise updates (eg. "Sending" -> "Sent" -> "Failed") without verbosity or repetition.
- Keep token surface area minimal: color/opacity/height tokens updated where necessary; avoid adding many new tokens unless justified.

Non-goals: Full redesign of button sizes or introducing new component variants. This ticket focuses on affordance + accessibility announcements and regression fixes for existing variants.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec (Figma) with skeleton state for all button variants: primary, secondary, ghost, icon-only, and split. Includes token references and motion timing.
Accessible announcement pattern documented: ARIA live region example markup/snippet, debounce rules to avoid repeated announcements, and guidance for screen reader verbosity.
Prototype (Figma & HTML/CSS) demonstrating no layout shift when switching to skeleton, with visual regression screenshots across themes (light/dark/high-contrast).
QA checklist: keyboard focus preserved, icon buttons announce action name + status, interrupted/canceled requests revert affordance cleanly and show error microcopy where applicable.
Design sign-off from Accessibility SIG and Product (comments resolved in PR).
Linked Engineering ticket created and dependency recorded for runtime changes required in button component library.
notes:
2026-02-10 — Created by Ava: initial problem summary and sketch attached. Suggested minimal token changes: button-skeleton-bg-opacity and skeleton-height-scale.

2026-02-16 — Review with Accessibility (Samir Patel): agreed on ARIA live polite region with short phrases and 200ms debounce; flagged that VoiceOver on iOS requires slightly longer timing for announcements — updated motion timing recommendation to 220ms fade-in for skeleton.

2026-02-20 — Design critique: prefer using existing brand tokens where possible; we added fallback rules for third-party themes. Action: produce visual regression snapshots for small/medium/large button sizes and icon-only.

2026-02-24 — Prototype branch opened (UX prototype + HTML/CSS). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/812 — includes lightweight CSS-only skeleton and ARIA example. Noted a browser bug: in Chrome on Android skeleton causes 1px text reflow when font-subpixel antialiasing toggles; engineering to patch via min-width enforcement.

2026-03-01 — PM feedback (Rhea Kumar): confirm behaviour for optimistic 'inline' responses (when UI updates before server ack). Decision: optimistic success flow should show a short green check microcopy and then replace skeleton with final state; failures revert to actionable error with retry affordance. Added acceptance criteria to cover optimistic flows.

Open follow-ups: update tokens backlog with token rename proposal to align with token discovery (see CON-DS-TOKENS-9). Schedule a short handoff session with eng on 2026-03-05.
qa_notes: Regression targets: mobile (iOS Safari, Chrome Android), desktop (Chrome/Firefox/Safari), screen readers (VoiceOver iOS, NVDA+Firefox, JAWS+Edge). Capture before/after screenshots with Percy. Confirm no new CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) reported in Lighthouse for pages using updated button component.
